article.title: Director Alex Gibney's Four Hour Doc 'Musk' Asks If Tech Mogul Is the 'Greatest Living Inventor' or a 'Fascist' Who 'Has Lost His Mind'
article.summary: VENICE, Italy (AP) — Alex Gibney has made films about powerful people, corporations and organizations before: Enron, Elizabeth Holmes, Scientology and the U.S. military’s abuses at Bagram and Abu Ghraib are just a few. And yet, he said, nothing compares to the scope of power held by his latest subject, Elon Musk.The postDirector Alex Gibney’s Four Hour Doc ‘Musk’ Asks If Tech Mogul Is the ‘Greatest Living Inventor’ or a ‘Fascist’ Who ‘Has Lost His Mind’appeared first onBreitbart.

article.title: Musk extremely dangerous for democracies around the world says Gibney in Venice
article.summary:
(ANSA) - ROME, 08 SET - Elon Musk is extremely dangerous for democracies around the world, Academy Award-winning US documentary maker Alex Gibney said in presenting his new documentary on the world's richest man at the Venice Film Festival on Tuesday.
New York-born Gibney, 72, won his Oscar in 2007 for Taxi to the Dark Side, focusing on a taxi driver in Afghanistan who was tortured and killed at Bagram Air Force Base in 2002. In 2010, Esquire magazine said he was "becoming the most important documentarian of our time."
Unveiling 'Musk', he said his subject's support for right-wing parties, from Germany to Turkey, from Great Britain to Brazil, "is linked to his ideology, but also to economic reasons. "Many of these right-wing governments tend to be more malleable. It's easier to achieve the desired results with totally corrupt and venal administrations, lacking self-control and internal oversight mechanisms. I think he's pursuing a global right-wing agenda." article.title: Elon Musk's MAGA-defecting ex claims she walked away from $40M to spill the dirt
article.summary: Elon Musk's ex, MAGA-defecting commentatorAshley St. Clair, says sheturned down $40 millionto stay quiet about the billionaire and chose to talk anyway.St. Clair, who shares a young son with Musk, his 13th child, revealed at the Venice Film Festival on Tuesday that she rejected an alleged $40 million nondisclosure agreement so she could sit for an interview in "Musk," a nearly four-hour documentary from Oscar-winning director Alex Gibney. The film premiered at the festival's 83rd edition, according to Variety."I was offered the opportunity not to speak for $40 million," St. Clair told reporters, saying the sum forced her to weigh what her voice was actually worth. She framed the choice as a lesson for her children that no amount of comfort should come before telling the truth.Now 28, St. Clair once built a following as aright-wing, anti-trans commentatorafter meeting Charlie Kirk at 18.
